st: Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C). Use a heavy Dutch oven with a tight lid in place of the traditional iron bell.
Pat the lamb and veal dry and season with [[2 tsp]] salt and [[1 tsp]] pepper.
Spread the potatoes, onions and carrots in the bottom of the Dutch oven and toss with half of the [[0.25 cup]] olive oil.
Nestle the meat on top of the vegetables and tuck in the [[6 clove]] garlic and [[4 sprig]] rosemary.
Drizzle with the remaining oil and pour in [[0.5 cup]] white wine or water around the edges.
Cover tightly and bake for 2 hours without opening the lid.
Uncover and bake 40 to 50 minutes more until the meat is very tender and the potatoes are browned at the edges.
Check that the lamb and veal are well above 145°F (63°C) inside and falling off the bone, then rest for 10 minutes.
Serve straight from the pot with the pan juices spooned over.

ing: cut into thin strips for larding
st: With a thin knife, poke deep slits all over the beef and push a strip of bacon and a slice of garlic into each (use [[4 clove]] garlic total).
Season the beef with [[1.5 tsp]] salt and [[1 tsp]] pepper.
Heat [[3 tbsp]] olive oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat and brown the beef on all sides, about 12 minutes. Move it to a plate.
Lower the heat to medium and cook the onions, carrots and celery for 8 minutes until soft.
Stir in [[2 tbsp]] tomato paste, the whole cloves and [[0.25 tsp]] nutmeg and cook 1 minute.
Return the beef, add [[2 cup]] red wine and enough water to come halfway up the meat.
Cover and simmer very gently for 2.5 hours, turning the beef every 30 minutes.
Add the [[8]] prunes and cook uncovered for 30 more minutes until the sauce thickens and the beef is fork tender.
Lift out the beef, pull out the cloves, and blend the sauce smooth with an immersion blender.
Slice the beef, boil the gnocchi according to the package, and serve the slices with gnocchi and plenty of sauce.

ing: body cut into rings, tentacles halved
st: Warm the [[5 cup]] stock in a saucepan and keep it at a low simmer.
Heat [[3 tbsp]] olive oil in a wide, heavy pan over medium heat and cook the onion for 5 minutes until soft.
Add the garlic and squid and cook for 5 minutes, stirring, until the squid turns opaque.
Stir in the [[1.5 cup]] rice and toast for 2 minutes.
Pour in [[0.5 cup]] wine and stir until it is absorbed.
Dissolve the [[4 g]] squid ink in a ladle of hot stock and stir it into the rice.
Add stock one ladle at a time, stirring often and waiting until each is absorbed before adding more. This takes about 20 minutes.
Taste the rice; it should be tender with a slight bite. Season with [[1 tsp]] salt and [[0.5 tsp]] pepper.
Rest off the heat for 2 minutes, stir in [[0.25 cup]] parsley and serve.

ing: melted, plus extra for the dish
st: Mix [[2.5 cup]] flour, [[0.5 tsp]] salt, 1 egg, [[1 tbsp]] oil and [[0.5 cup]] warm water into a soft dough. Knead 8 minutes until smooth.
Cover the dough and rest it for 30 minutes.
For the filling, mix the [[2 cup]] cottage cheese, 2 eggs, [[0.5 cup]] sour cream and [[0.5 tsp]] salt.
Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C) and butter a baking dish.
Roll the dough on a floured towel as thin as you can, to roughly a 16 by 20 inch rectangle.
Spread the filling over the dough, then use the towel to roll it up like a jelly roll. Cut into 2 inch pieces.
Stand the pieces upright, snug together, in the dish. Brush with [[4 tbsp]] melted butter.
Whisk 1 egg with [[1 cup]] sour cream and pour over the top.
Bake for 35 minutes until golden and set. Rest 5 minutes before serving.
Heat [[2 tbsp]] oil in a skillet and cook the onion and bacon for 8 minutes until soft. Stir in [[1 tbsp]] paprika and cool.
In a bowl, combine the onion mixture, [[1.5 lb]] pork, [[0.5 cup]] rice, [[1 tsp]] salt and [[1 tsp]] pepper.
If the cabbage leaves are very salty, soak them in cold water for 20 minutes. Trim any thick ribs.
Place a heaping spoonful of filling near the stem end of a leaf, fold in the sides, and roll up tightly.
Spread [[1 cup]] of the sauerkraut over the bottom of a large pot and add the ribs, if using.
Pack the rolls in tight layers, tucking in [[2 bay leaves]] and the remaining sauerkraut.
Add water just to cover, put a plate on top to hold the rolls down, and bring to a boil.
Cover and simmer on low for 2 hours until the pork is cooked to at least 160°F (71°C) and the rice is soft.
Serve warm with some of the cooking liquid.

ing: such as cod or halibut, cut in large pieces
st: Heat [[0.25 cup]] olive oil in a wide pot over medium heat. Cook the onions for 10 minutes until golden.
Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Pour in [[0.5 cup]] wine and let it bubble for 2 minutes.
Add the tomatoes, [[1]] bay leaf, [[1 tsp]] salt and [[0.5 tsp]] pepper. Simmer for 15 minutes until thick.
Meanwhile, bring [[4 cup]] water and [[0.5 tsp]] salt to a boil and slowly whisk in [[1 cup]] polenta. Cook on low, stirring often, for 25 minutes.
Lay the fish in the sauce, cover, and cook gently for 8 to 10 minutes until it flakes.
Scatter [[0.25 cup]] parsley on top and serve over the polenta.
Mix [[3 cup]] flour, [[1 tsp]] salt, [[1 cup]] warm water and [[2 tbsp]] olive oil into a smooth dough. Knead 5 minutes and rest 30 minutes.
Toss the chopped chard with [[1 tsp]] salt and squeeze out as much liquid as you can.
Mix the chard with the onions, garlic, [[0.5 cup]] parsley, [[0.25 cup]] olive oil and [[0.5 tsp]] pepper.
Heat the oven to 475°F (245°C) with a baking sheet inside.
Divide the dough in two and roll each piece paper thin, about 12 inches across.
Spread the filling over one piece to within an inch of the edge, cover with the second piece, and seal and crimp the edges.
Prick the top a few times and brush with [[2 tbsp]] olive oil.
Slide onto the hot sheet and bake 15 to 18 minutes until browned in spots.
Brush with the remaining oil and cut into wedges.
Soak [[0.5 cup]] raisins in [[2 tbsp]] rum or orange juice for 15 minutes.
Whisk 2 eggs with [[0.25 cup]] sugar and [[0.75 cup]] milk.
Stir in [[2 cup]] flour, [[2 tsp]] baking powder, [[0.25 tsp]] salt and [[1 tbsp]] lemon zest until it forms a thick, sticky batter.
Fold in the raisins and any liquid left in the bowl.
Heat [[3 cup]] oil in a deep pot to 350°F (175°C).
Drop in rounded teaspoons of batter, 6 or so at a time, and fry 3 to 4 minutes, turning, until deep golden.
Drain on paper towels and let the oil come back to temperature between batches.
Dust with [[0.25 cup]] powdered sugar and serve warm.
Heat the oven to 325°F (160°C). Set six ramekins in a deep baking pan.
Cook [[0.5 cup]] sugar with [[2 tbsp]] water in a saucepan over medium heat, without stirring, until deep amber, about 8 minutes. Pour into the ramekins at once.
Warm [[2.5 cup]] milk with [[1 tsp]] lemon zest until steaming, not boiling.
Whisk 4 eggs, 1 yolk, [[0.25 cup]] sugar, [[1 tsp]] vanilla and a pinch of salt in a bowl.
Slowly pour the warm milk into the eggs while whisking. Stir in [[1 tbsp]] rum if using.
Strain into the ramekins.
Pour hot water into the pan to come halfway up the ramekins.
Bake 35 to 40 minutes until set with a slight wobble in the center.
Cool, then chill at least 6 hours.
Run a knife around each custard and flip onto a plate so the caramel pours over.

ing: fresh, shaved or grated, or 1 tbsp truffle paste
st: Bring a large pot of water to a boil and add [[1 tbsp]] salt.
Cook the pasta 1 minute less than the package says, about 10 minutes.
Scoop out [[0.5 cup]] of pasta water, then drain.
In a wide skillet, melt [[3 tbsp]] butter over medium-low heat. Add [[0.75 cup]] cream and simmer 3 minutes.
Toss in the pasta with [[0.5 cup]] Parmesan and a splash of pasta water until creamy.
Season with [[0.25 tsp]] pepper and shave half of the [[1 oz]] truffle in. Stir off the heat.
Plate and top with the rest of the truffle.
Heat the oven to 475°F (245°C), or use a grill. Line a baking sheet with foil.
Roast the whole peppers and eggplant, turning every 10 minutes, until the skins are blackened, about 40 minutes.
Put the vegetables in a covered bowl for 15 minutes so they steam.
Peel off the skins and remove the stems and seeds from the peppers. Scoop out the eggplant flesh.
Chop the vegetables finely or pulse in a food processor to a chunky purée.
Heat [[0.25 cup]] oil in a wide pot, add the purée and cook over medium-low heat for 25 minutes, stirring often, until thick.
Stir in the garlic, [[1.5 tsp]] salt, [[1 tbsp]] vinegar and the remaining oil. Cook 5 more minutes.
Cool and store in clean jars in the fridge for up to 2 weeks.
